messages:
Sam (support): Hey team, incoming from ACME: sudden spike in p95/p99 latencies for Dedicated pool 'eu-dedicated-3' around 04:15 UTC, started after their large batch onboarding. Customer sees 5-10x p99 and ~20% 500s. Escalating, can we triage?
Priya (eng-oncall): Thanks Sam. Do we have a repro or request IDs? Any recent deploys? :thinking_face:
Sam (support): Customer supplied sample request IDs and a short curl repro. They also included a screenshot of spikes aligned with scale-up events. No platform deploys between 03:30-05:00.
Sam (support): curl repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-ACME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-16k","input":"ping"}'
```
Ken (eng-sre): Pulling logs for eu-dedicated-3. I see a bunch of attach retries and long warmup durations: `gpu_coldstart_seconds` samples around 48-75s. Also `attach_latency` spikes to 30-120s during the window.
ops-bot: Incident alert: scaleup_attach_failures >= 5 in 10m for eu-dedicated-3.
Priya (eng-oncall): Ok that matches customer timeline. Two hypotheses: (1) Dedicated pool saturated -> queueing + warmups; (2) Auth or agent-level throttling causing attach_retry loops. Any 401/5xx pattern?
Ken (eng-sre): Logs show a handful of 403/401 from image pull auth rotation around 04:12 but only 3-4 of those; majority are attach timeouts: `attach_request timeout after 60s` and subsequent retry backoffs. Heap of concurrent attach requests ~= 140 while pool capacity is 96. That's classic scale-up lag + cold GPU start.
Marta (eng-platform): On platform side, autoscale backoff throttle configured to protect infra under flood; I see the scale-up controller hit a soft limit when simultaneous attach rate > 100 and applied 6s randomized backoff, which amplified the attach queue. Also the min_pool for this customer was 0.
Sam (support): Customer requests immediate mitigation — they want latency restored asap. What can we do right now?
Priya (eng-oncall): Short-term playbook: 1) Temporarily route ACME to a satellite fallback pool (shared) to drop p99 while we fix dedicated pool; 2) Bump min_pool to 2 for eu-dedicated-3 for next hour; 3) Disable aggressive attach backoff for that pool (riskier) or increase upper bound; 4) Ask customer to throttle onboarding ramp if possible.
Ken (eng-sre): I'll run a quick patch: set pool.min = 2 and disable randomized backoff for that pool. That should open capacity and reduce attach fanout. Also I'll create a temporary policy to prefer shared fallback for their API key.
Marta (eng-platform): I'll open a fast path to prewarm images: trigger `prewarm_pool(eu-dedicated-3, 10)` and kick off model cache prefetch for their model variant. Also I'll push a short-term autoscaler tweak: increase scale_up_grace_seconds from 20 -> 90 for this pool so it doesn't oscillate and cause thundering attach.
Sam (support): Passing actions to ACME; they accepted fallback to shared and slowed their onboarding ramp.
ops-bot: Action log: prewarm initiated by Marta at 04:28 UTC; pool.min updated by Ken at 04:29 UTC; fallback policy applied by Ken at 04:31 UTC.
Priya (eng-oncall): For root cause follow-up: we should verify image-pull auth rotation and analyze why coldstart was 48-75s (kernel load vs model I/O). Ken can capture node-level timings. Also add a metric dashboard: p99_attach_time, pool_active_requests, pool_available_gpus, image_pull_latency.
Ken (eng-sre): Will correlate kube events and node logs. Preliminary note: two nodes exhibited high disk pressure and slow image unpack (nvml reports show slower than baseline). Might be transient infra degradation.
Marta (eng-platform): Longer term mitigations: - enforce non-zero min_pool for customers ramping > 50 qps - proactive prewarm during billing/onboarding windows - add jittered but bounded backoff and circuit-breaker that routes to fallback earlier - detect sudden attach fanout and auto-enable prewarm
Priya (eng-oncall): Customer impact update: After fallback and prewarm, p95 returned to normal within ~8 minutes, p99 improved but still a bit elevated while remaining attach queue drains. Customer confirmed degraded but acceptable. :white_check_mark:
Sam (support): Customer thanked the team and asked for a postmortem and preventive steps. Can we make a short blameless postmortem and a one-time credit?
Priya (eng-oncall): Yes. Ken + Marta — please prepare a short postmortem with timeline, root cause, and the three platform changes (min_pool guard, prewarm automation, backoff bounds). Support will draft the customer communication and credit.
Ken (eng-sre): On it. I'll attach node timelines and samples of `attach_request` logs and prom queries. Sample PromQL to reproduce the spike view:
```
sum(rate(attach_request_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="eu-dedicated-3"}[5m])) by (le)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(attach_request_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="eu-dedicated-3"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Marta (eng-platform): Also adding an alert: if attach_queue_length > 50 AND pool_available_gpus < 0.5 -> auto-enable fallback and prewarm.
Priya (eng-oncall): Great. Closing loop: immediate mitigations done, customer stable, documenting postmortem and runway fixes. Thanks all. :rocket:
